title: The incremental conjecture for set multipartite Ramsey numbers
source: Claudia J. F. Gonçalves, Emerson L. Monte Carmelo and Irene N. Nakaoka, “Projective planes and set multipartite Ramsey numbers for C_4 versus star”, arXiv:1710.06383 (2017). https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.06383
statement:
Let $s\geq 2$ and $n\geq 2$ be integers. For positive integers $s,n$, let $M_s(n)$ denote the set multipartite Ramsey number for $C_4$ versus the star $K_{1,n}$, namely the least $c$ such that every spanning subgraph $G$ of the complete balanced $s$-partite graph $K_{c\times s}$ contains a copy of $C_4$ or its complement contains a copy of $K_{1,n}$. **Incremental conjecture.** For any integers $s\geq 2$ and $n\geq 2$, 
$$
M_s(n+1)\leq M_s(n)+1.
$$
 The preceding proposition proves this bound under an additional numerical hypothesis; the conjecture asserts that the hypothesis can be removed.
summary: For all s >= 2 and n >= 2, M_s(n+1) <= M_s(n) + 1, where M_s(n) is the least positive c such that every spanning subgraph G of the complete multipartite graph with c classes of s vertices either contains a 4-cycle or leaves some vertex with at least n non-neighbours in other classes (a star K_{1,n} in the complement relative to the host). This is Conjecture 2.3 of Goncalves, Monte Carmelo and Nakaoka, who proved the inequality only under an additional numerical hypothesis by keeping the original partition. The proof here proves the stronger step that the property at (n, c) implies the property at (n+1, c+1) by abandoning the partition: delete s suitable vertices and re-partition the rest into c independent s-sets, by a one-vertex swap forced by C4-freeness when s >= 3, and for s = 2 by a friendship-type lemma (two vertices with no common neighbour) with a perfect matching in the complement, plus explicit small cases. Lean defines the host graph, the property and the minimum literally, and proves that the minimum exists.
paste_summary: Proved. For all s >= 2 and n >= 2, M_s(n+1) <= M_s(n) + 1 for the set-multipartite Ramsey number of C_4 against the star K_{1,n} (c classes of s vertices). This is Conjecture 2.3 of Goncalves, Monte Carmelo and Nakaoka, proved in the source only under an extra hypothesis.
